conventions.convention: Fourier transform normalization is the negative-sign, 2π-normalized convention f-hat(ξ) = ∫ f(x) exp(-2πi x·ξ) dx, evaluated pointwise at every frequency on L1 classes (not defined only a.e.), with the inverse integral using +2πi x·ξ and no 1/(2π)^n factor.

Convolution is (f*g)(x) = ∫ f(x-y) g(y) dy, so convolution transforms to the pointwise product and the product to the convolution of transforms; the value of a convolution on its null exceptional set is irrelevant.

The L2 inner product is linear in the first variable, <f,g> = ∫ f conj(g), and the Cauchy-Schwarz equality criterion is stated for the second argument nonzero: equality iff f = c g a.e., with a common scalar across components in the finite-tuple version.

A topological vector space is a vector space with jointly continuous addition and scalar multiplication; Hausdorffness is a separate hypothesis, a zero-neighborhood need not be open, and the zero space with its unique topology is allowed.

Convexity is defined with real coefficients even over C; balanced means |λ| ≤ 1 implies λC ⊆ C; a set is absolutely convex when convex and balanced, and local convexity means every zero-neighborhood contains a convex one (equivalently an open convex zero-neighborhood base).

HB (the real dominated-extension principle) is an additional principle over ZF, explicitly assumed by each separation theorem and by nothing in the topology/gauge suppliers; the separation inequality is stated as Re f(a) < α ≤ Re f(b), strict on the open side, and strict on both sides when both sets are open.

Choice accounting is local: measure/integration and approximation arguments assume countable choice (stated in each item), the finite-measure smoothing and measure-uniqueness results assume full AC via Radon-Nikodym and Hahn/Jordan, and the elementary product/TVS, cutoff and Gaussian-support arguments are choice-free.

Schwartz space consists of actual C-infinity functions (not classes) with sup_x |x^alpha d^beta f(x)| finite for all multi-indices, topologized by finitely many seminorm constraints; convergence is convergence in every seminorm.
A 'face' of a convex set is a convex subset with the endpoint property; the endpoint property alone is called extremal, so the maximum set {-1,1} of t^2 on [-1,1] is extremal but not a face.
Sums over Z^n are limits over increasing integer cubes, with absolute convergence making the ordering immaterial; the periodization tiling uses the half-open cube [0,1)^n.

Lebesgue-point recovery is stated with the specified Lebesgue value a, i.e. A(r) = ∫_{|y|<r}|f(x-y)-a| dy = o(r^n), not with an arbitrary value of a chosen representative; the kernel is normalized as ε^{-n} K(y/ε) with ∫K = 1 and |K(y)| ≤ Φ(|y|) for a bounded nonincreasing integrable radial majorant.
The characteristic-function convention phi_mu(t) = ∫ e^{it·x} dmu(x) is related to the measure transform by phi_mu(t) = mu-hat(-t/(2π)), a sign-and-scale dictionary only.

load_bearing.statement: Assume countable choice. Fourier transformation on Schwartz space extends uniquely to a surjective complex-linear isometry F_2 : L^2(R^n;C) -> L^2(R^n;C). It preserves the first-variable-linear inner product, and hence is unitary.

For f in L^1(R^n;C), n >= 1, f-hat(ξ) = F f(ξ) := ∫ f(x) exp(-2πi x·ξ) dx, ξ in R^n; the integral is read on any measurable representative and the output is a function defined at every frequency, not merely an almost-everywhere class.
For every f in L^1(R^n;C), n >= 1, the integral defining f-hat(ξ) is absolutely convergent for every ξ and unchanged by null-set modifications. Moreover |f-hat(ξ)| <= ||f||_1.

Assume HB. Let A, B be nonempty disjoint convex subsets of a real or complex TVS X, and suppose A is open. There are a nonzero continuous K-linear functional f and α in R such that Re f(a) < α <= Re f(b) for a in A, b in B. If B is also open, the same α may be chosen with both pointwise inequalities strict. Neither Hausdorffness nor local convexity beyond the given open convex set is needed.
Assume countable choice. The negative-sign, 2π-normalized Fourier transform is continuous F : S -> S, and F(d^α f)(ξ) = (2πiξ)^α f-hat(ξ), d^β f-hat = F((-2πi x)^β f).
Assume countable choice. For every f in S(R^n) and every x in R^n, f(x) = ∫ f-hat(ξ) exp(2πi x·ξ) dξ. The integral is absolutely convergent.
Assume countable choice. For n >= 1, t > 0, and ξ in R^n, F(exp(-πt|x|^2))(ξ) = t^{-n/2} exp(-π|ξ|^2/t). Every polynomial times a positive real Gaussian is absolutely integrable.
Assume countable choice. For f, g in S(R^n), ∫ f-hat(ξ) conj(g-hat(ξ)) dξ = ∫ f(x) conj(g(x)) dx. The pairing is complex-linear in the first variable. In particular ||f-hat||_2 = ||f||_2.
Assume countable choice. If f is in S(R^n), then x^α d^β f is in L^p for every 1 <= p <= infinity and every α, β. Its norm is bounded by a finite sum of Schwartz seminorms.

Assume countable choice. If f is in L^1(R^n;C) and f-hat is in L^1, then g(x) = ∫ f-hat(ξ) exp(2πi x·ξ) dξ is bounded and continuous, equals f almost everywhere, and equals the specified value at every Lebesgue point of f.
Assume countable choice. If f, g are in L^1(R^n;C), n >= 1, then the transform of f*g equals f-hat times g-hat at every ξ in R^n.

Let U be an open convex zero-neighborhood in a real or complex TVS. Its gauge p = p_U is finite, nonnegative, subadditive, positively real-homogeneous and continuous. Moreover U = {x : p(x) < 1}. If U is balanced then p(λx) = |λ| p(x) for every scalar, so p is a continuous seminorm; it need not be positive definite.

For every zero-neighborhood U in a locally convex real or complex TVS, there is an open balanced convex zero-neighborhood V with closure(V) contained in U. Consequently U contains a closed balanced convex zero-neighborhood. No Hausdorffness, Hahn-Banach or choice principle is assumed.

Assume countable choice. For complex C^1 functions u, v on [a,b], a < b, ∫ u'v = u(b)v(b) - u(a)v(a) - ∫ uv' and ∫ u' = u(b) - u(a); if u, v are C^1 on R with u'v, uv' in L^1 and u(x)v(x) -> 0 as x -> ±infinity, then ∫ u'v = -∫ uv'.

Assume countable choice. Let K be measurable with ∫K = 1 and |K(y)| <= Φ(|y|), where Φ is bounded, nonincreasing and ∫Φ(|y|)dy < infinity. For f in L^1 and a point x with specified Lebesgue value a, ∫ ε^{-n} K(y/ε) f(x-y) dy -> a as ε decreases to 0.

concerns.concern: Step 2.1 asserts that 'continuity of the exponential at zero gives a single δ>0 such that |h|<δ implies |exp(-2πix·h)-1| < ε/(2(1+||f||_1))' for all |x| ≤ R. Continuity of (x,h) -> exp(-2πix·h) at h=0 alone gives only a δ depending on x; uniformity over the compact slice |x| ≤ R is the extra step (Heine-Cantor on the box, or the bound |exp(iθ)-1| ≤ |θ| ≤ 2πR|h|). The cited facts F2/F3/F4 do not supply it and the item does not name it.

Step 1.1 derives ∫exp(-πx^2)dx = 1 from the cited ∫exp(-x^2)dx = sqrt(π) without displaying the rescaling substitution, and compresses the majorant bound |x|^m exp(-cx^2) <= C exp(-cx^2/2) into 'F3 bounds ... on the tails' plus continuity on a compact middle. Both are immediate, but they are steps the reader must reconstruct rather than read.

seams_checked.note: Every citing item I located was opened and compared against my statements. def-carleson-operator-and-measurable-linearisation uses the pointwise L1 transform, absolute convergence and representative independence, and 'f, f-hat in L1' for Schwartz f: these are exactly def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn, lem-l-one-fourier-transform-is-well-defined, thm-fourier-transform-maps-schwartz-space-continuously-to-itself and lem-schwartz-functions-and-all-derivatives-are-integrable. def-carleson-tiles-wave-packets-and-tile-order uses pointwise Schwartz inversion and the translation/modulation/dilation laws with the same negative 2π normalization and the |det A|^{-1} dilation convention; the packet formula it derives matches f-hat(ξ)=|I_s|^{1/2}exp(-2πi c(I_s)(ξ-c(ω_{s,-})))ψ(|I_s|(ξ-c(ω_{s,-}))), which I recomputed from my laws. lem-carleson-size-selection, lem-carleson-single-tree-estimate and lem-carleson-signed-tree-weak-one-one-estimate cite 'Plancherel preserves the complex inner product' and assume AC, which implies the countable-choice hypothesis of thm-plancherel; lem-carleson-single-tree-estimate also cites the Schwartz convolution/product law and pointwise Schwartz inversion. thm-carleson-maximal-operator-is-strong-ltwo cites 'Schwartz classes are dense in complex L2 under countable choice', which is lem-schwartz-space-is-dense-in-l-two verbatim in content. No domain, quantifier, hypothesis, direction or conclusion is strengthened or weakened in any of these citations.

rem-characteristic-function-fourier-stieltjes-convention states the convention of thm-fourier-transform-of-a-finite-complex-measure as mu-hat(ξ)=∫exp(-2πix·ξ)dμ(x) and converts it to phi_mu(t)=mu-hat(-t/(2π)); it retains my countable-choice hypothesis for the transform theorem and does not claim the probability-law identity needs more. thm-uniqueness-of-a-law-from-its-characteristic-function and thm-cramer-wold-device cite cor-uniqueness-of-finite-borel-measures-from-their-fourier-transforms as 'under AC finite complex Borel measures with equal transforms are equal' / 'AC gives uniqueness of finite-variation Borel measures in every positive finite dimension'; that is exactly the corollary's statement (n >= 1, finite total variation, equal transforms). Both consumer items assume AC and apply it in dimension one/d, as the corollary permits.
